dataset: Alarm logs of industrial packaging machines
source: University of Padua Research Data record 1031 / DOI 10.21227/nfv6-k750
license: CC BY 4.0, recorded separately for the data archive, code archive, and README on the official repository page

parsed_source.note: The provider README says both X and Y have length 109, but the downloaded NPZ has 556 output columns. This inconsistency is preserved; the pilot below used raw alarms.csv rather than the supplied processed split.

pilot.task: Six-hour per-alarm count vector -> binary label indicating at least one alarm in the next hour
pilot.architecture: plain dense TabularMLP; no recurrence, convolution, attention, embedding, or class balancing
pilot.split: Group-disjoint machines using NumPy RNG seed 20261023; train serials [0,2,5,6,7,8,10,12,13,14,15,16], validation [1,4,18,19], test [3,9,11,17]
pilot.preprocessing: Counts standardized with training examples only; full training split in one batch; no windows cross machine groups.
pilot.training: CUDA RTX 3050 Laptop 6 GiB; Adam 1e-3; cross-entropy; seed 20261023+j; 30 full-batch epochs; validation minimum cross-entropy selects checkpoint; test touched once per configuration.

disposition: KEEP PROVISIONALLY as a non-saturated supervised event-occurrence stress task only. Open access, CC BY 4.0, fixed-width MLP compatibility, group split, and whole-batch fit were verified. The test group's event rate differs greatly from validation, and simple previous-hour persistence beats every tested MLP; do not treat this as a strong predictive benchmark without a better task/protocol. The provider's next-alarm-type and multi-label future-alarm tasks were not MLP-piloted; the supplied sequence targets have a README/NPZ length mismatch and need a separate screen. This is not runner-integrated. Only three vanilla architectures, one group split and one seed were piloted; no ADP variants or full vanilla grid were tested.
